title: How to Get Your Brand Mentioned in ChatGPT: 7 Practical Steps
excerpt: How to get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT: make your site eligible for ChatGPT search, publish clear answers, earn reviews and coverage, and measure mentions over time.
keywords: get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT
author: AI Brand Track Team
content:
To get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT, make sure ChatGPT search can crawl and understand your site, publish clear pages that answer the questions buyers actually ask, and build a consistent presence on third-party sources such as review sites, comparison articles, news coverage, reference sites and community discussions. Then measure your mentions with repeated prompt tests so you know what is working. There is no shortcut, and no paid placement inside the answers ([OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt) ads don't influence them). No one can guarantee a timeline, but these steps improve your odds in both live search answers and future training data.

## How ChatGPT decides which brands to mention

ChatGPT's brand recommendations come from two main places:

- **Training data.** OpenAI's help article on [how ChatGPT and its foundation models are developed](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) says its models learn from publicly available internet content, data accessed through third-party partners, and information provided or generated by users, human trainers and researchers. In our view, brands that are discussed often and consistently in that material are more likely to come up. This source changes only when newer models are released.
- **Live web search.** ChatGPT can search the web and cite the pages it used. According to OpenAI's [help article on searching the web with ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), it may search automatically when a question would benefit from current information. Changes to your site and to third-party coverage can show up here much sooner.

So getting mentioned is less about one tactic and more about being well represented across the public web, on pages ChatGPT can retrieve. For a deeper explanation, see [where does ChatGPT get its information?](/blog/where-does-chatgpt-get-its-information)

## Why it matters

Buyers can ask AI assistants for recommendations: "What's the best project management software for a small agency?", "Which CRM should I choose?", "Top email marketing platforms for small business?" When ChatGPT answers, in our testing it typically names a handful of brands. If you are not among them, you are not part of that buyer's shortlist.

Unlike a search results page, ChatGPT does not show a fixed list of ten links. In our testing, answers vary from run to run, and features like [ChatGPT memory](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt) can make them differ from person to person (we explain why in [does ChatGPT give the same answer to everyone?](/blog/does-chatgpt-give-the-same-answer-to-everyone)), so the goal is to appear consistently, not just once.

## How to check whether ChatGPT mentions you today

Start with a baseline before changing anything:

1. **Write 15-30 buyer-style prompts.** Category prompts ("best [category] tools for [audience]"), comparison prompts ("[you] vs [competitor]"), problem prompts ("how do I [job your product does]") and branded prompts ("what is [your brand]?").
2. **Use clean sessions.** Test logged out, or in a [Temporary Chat](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046-temporary-chat-in-chatgpt) set to Unpersonalized, so your own chat history and memory don't skew results. Use a fresh chat for every prompt.
3. **Run each prompt several times.** Because answers vary, a single run proves little. Note how many runs mention you.
4. **Log the details.** Whether you were mentioned, your position in the list, how you were described, which competitors appeared and which sources were cited.
5. **Repeat on other assistants.** Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini are separate systems and can give different answers.

Our guide to [tracking brand mentions in ChatGPT](/blog/how-to-track-chatgpt-brand-mentions) includes a full prompt set and logging template.

## The 7 steps to get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT

### Step 1: Make sure ChatGPT search can find and understand your site

OpenAI's [crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) explains that OAI-SearchBot is the crawler used to surface websites in ChatGPT's search features, and that sites opted out of it will not be shown in ChatGPT search answers (though they can still appear as navigational links). [OpenAI's search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt) adds that to make a site eligible, you should allow OAI-SearchBot and make sure your host or CDN allows traffic from OpenAI's published search-bot IP addresses. Placement is not guaranteed, but blocking it rules you out.

Practical checks:

- Review robots.txt for rules that block OAI-SearchBot. Decide separately whether to allow GPTBot, which [OpenAI says](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) crawls content that may be used for training. The two settings are independent.
- Make sure important pages return their main content in the HTML, not only after heavy client-side scripts run.
- Keep pages indexable, fast and free of broken links.

### Step 2: Publish clear pages that answer buyer questions

ChatGPT can only describe you accurately if the facts are easy to find. Make sure your site clearly states:

- What you do and who it is for, in plain language
- Pricing (or how pricing works)
- Key features and use cases
- How you compare to the main alternatives
- Where you operate, if location matters

Then build pages around the real questions buyers ask: "best X for Y", "X vs Y", "how much does X cost", "how to solve [problem]". Use descriptive headings, short answer-first paragraphs, lists and tables. Original data, detailed guides and honest comparison pages give other sites a reason to reference you. Keep content updated so retrieved pages don't contradict your current offer. This is the core of [generative engine optimization](/generative-engine-optimization), and our [how to rank on ChatGPT](/how-to-rank-on-chatgpt) playbook goes step by step.

### Step 3: Earn coverage and links from trusted publications

In our experience, search answers often lean on pages other than your own site, and training data draws on [publicly available internet content](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed), so how widely and consistently you are discussed matters. Earned coverage helps on both fronts:

- Pitch original data, research and expert commentary to journalists and industry publications.
- Announce genuinely newsworthy milestones: launches, research releases, notable partnerships.
- Contribute guest articles and expert quotes to respected trade publications in your niche.
- Make sure coverage uses your brand name clearly and consistently.

Relevance matters more than volume. A few mentions in publications your buyers actually read are worth more than many low-quality links. Avoid paid link schemes and spammy directories; they add little and can damage trust.

### Step 4: Get your facts right on reference sites and knowledge bases

Wikipedia and similar reference sources are part of the publicly available web, so accuracy there matters. If your organization genuinely meets Wikipedia's [notability guideline for organizations and companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Notability_%28organizations_and_companies%29), which requires significant coverage in independent, reliable sources, a page may be appropriate. Wikipedia's [conflict of interest guideline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Conflict_of_interest) strongly discourages editing articles about your own company; the accepted route is to suggest changes on the article's talk page and disclose your connection.

Beyond Wikipedia:

- Keep your name, address, phone number and description consistent across business directories and profiles.
- Make sure industry databases, marketplace listings and partner directories describe you accurately.
- Fix outdated pages that still show old pricing, old product names or a previous brand.

### Step 5: Build a strong presence on review and comparison sites

In our testing, for commercial questions the sources cited in ChatGPT search answers often include review platforms, directories and "best of" comparison articles. To find out which ones matter in your category, run your buyer prompts with search on and note which domains appear in the [Sources panel](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt).

Then:

- Claim and complete your profiles on the review platforms relevant to your category (for software that might be G2 or Capterra; for local businesses, Google Business Profile and industry directories).
- Ask satisfied customers for reviews on a steady basis and respond to reviews professionally.
- Fill in descriptions, features, pricing and use cases so the profile answers buyer questions on its own.
- Reach out to authors of comparison articles that are cited for your category and offer accurate information, a demo or a trial so they can evaluate you.

### Step 6: Show up where your category is discussed

Brands become familiar through their wider network, not just their own site:

- Take part in community discussions, forums and Q&A sites where buyers ask for recommendations, and contribute genuinely useful answers rather than promotion.
- Get listed on partner pages and integration directories where you have real partnerships.
- Join relevant industry associations and appear at events, podcasts and webinars.
- Co-create content with complementary brands.

Each of these creates more independent, consistent descriptions of what you do, which adds to the [publicly available content](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7842364-how-chatgpt-and-our-foundation-models-are-developed) models learn from and the pages search can retrieve.

### Step 7: Measure your AI visibility over time

You can't improve what you don't measure. Re-run your prompt set on a regular schedule (monthly is a sensible baseline; more often while you are actively working on visibility) and track:

- **Mention rate:** the share of runs in which your brand appears
- **Position:** whether you are named first or near the end of a list
- **Share of voice:** your mentions compared with competitors on the same prompts
- **Sentiment and accuracy:** how you are described, and whether the facts are right
- **Cited sources:** which pages ChatGPT relies on for your category

Look for changes that hold across several rounds rather than reacting to one result. If a model update reshuffles results, our guide to [AI model drift detection](/blog/ai-model-drift-detection) explains how to spot it.

## How long does it take to get mentioned in ChatGPT?

There is no reliable fixed timeline, and anyone promising one is guessing. It depends on which source drives the answer:

- **Search-enabled answers** can reflect improvements once your new or updated pages, reviews and coverage are crawled and start being retrieved. In our experience that can be a matter of weeks, but it varies by category and competition. [OpenAI notes](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots) that changes to robots.txt rules for OAI-SearchBot take about 24 hours to be picked up.
- **Answers based on training data** change only when OpenAI releases newer models trained on more recent data, which can take months.

In our experience, brands that already have strong coverage and reviews tend to see changes sooner than brands starting from scratch. Consistent effort over months matters more than one big push.

## What content types tend to earn mentions?

- **Original research and data** that others cite
- **Comprehensive guides** that answer a buyer's question fully
- **Honest comparison pages** ("X vs Y", "alternatives to X")
- **Case studies** with concrete, verifiable details
- **Clear product, pricing and FAQ pages** that state facts plainly
- **Expert commentary** quoted in third-party publications

The common thread is content that other sites want to reference and that ChatGPT search can quote directly.

## Mistakes that keep brands out of ChatGPT answers

- **Blocking OAI-SearchBot** in robots.txt or at the CDN level, often by accident.
- **Inconsistent naming and facts** across your site, profiles and directories.
- **Vague positioning** that never says plainly what you do and for whom.
- **Relying only on your own site** with little independent coverage or reviews.
- **Testing once from your own account** and drawing conclusions from a single, personalized answer.
- **Giving up too early** before search or model updates have had time to reflect changes.
- **Ignoring other assistants.** Claude, Perplexity and Gemini can surface different brands than ChatGPT.

## How do other AI assistants compare?

ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google Gemini each use their own models, their own search or retrieval systems and their own update schedules. Visibility on one does not guarantee visibility on another, and you may rank well in one assistant and be missing from the next. Perplexity, for example, [surfaces and links websites in its search results](https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots), so the pages it retrieves matter a lot there; see our [Perplexity SEO](/perplexity-seo) guide.

The good news is that the fundamentals overlap: crawlable pages, clear facts and strong third-party coverage help everywhere. Measuring all four side by side shows where your gaps are. Our guide on [how to track brand visibility across AI platforms](/blog/how-to-track-brand-visibility-in-ai-platforms) covers the multi-platform approach.

## Does your industry matter?

Your category affects how often ChatGPT names specific brands. In our experience, questions about software, consumer products and services often produce lists of named brands, while some topics, such as personal health or financial decisions, tend to get more general, cautious answers. Categories with many competitors are harder to break into than niche ones.

Whatever your industry, the approach is the same: find the prompts your buyers use, see who gets named today, and close the gap with the steps above.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does it cost to get your brand mentioned in ChatGPT?

You cannot pay OpenAI for a mention inside ChatGPT's answers; [OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt) ads do not influence them. The cost is the time and budget you put into your website, content, PR, reviews and measurement, which varies widely by company and category. You can get a baseline with AI Brand Track's 14-day trial for $9 (1 full analysis plus weekly checks of 1 brand).

### Can you pay ChatGPT to mention your brand?

Not in the answers themselves. OpenAI began testing ads in ChatGPT in the US in February 2026 for users on the Free and Go plans and is expanding gradually, but according to its [ads help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt), ads appear separately below the response, are clearly labeled, and do not influence ChatGPT's answers. Advertisers have no ability to shape, rank or alter responses. Organic mentions depend on your public footprint and on the pages ChatGPT retrieves.

### How often should you check if ChatGPT mentions your brand?

Monthly is a sensible baseline. Check more often while you are actively working on visibility, and right after a product launch, rebrand or major ChatGPT model release. Because answers vary, compare results across several rounds before drawing conclusions.

### Do ChatGPT mentions translate to sales?

They can, if buyers use AI assistants to build shortlists, but the effect is hard to measure directly and varies by category. Watch for referral traffic from ChatGPT in your analytics, ask new customers how they found you, and track your mention rate alongside these signals.

### What's the difference between SEO and optimizing for ChatGPT mentions?

Classic SEO aims to rank pages in search results. Optimizing for ChatGPT aims to have your brand named and described accurately in generated answers. They overlap a lot: crawlable, clear, helpful pages and strong third-party coverage help both. The differences are that AI answers summarize several sources, rarely show a fixed ranking, and vary between runs, so you measure mention rates rather than positions. See [GEO vs SEO vs AEO](/blog/geo-vs-seo-vs-aeo) for more.

### Can negative content affect ChatGPT mentions?

Yes. ChatGPT can reflect how sources describe you, so widespread negative reviews or coverage can show up in how you are described or whether you are recommended. Respond to problems openly, fix the underlying issues, and keep accurate, positive information visible on the sources that get cited.

### How do you get ChatGPT to mention your brand for specific queries?

Focus on the problem and use case behind the query. Publish pages that answer that question directly, earn coverage that positions you for that use case, and get included in the comparison articles and reviews that ChatGPT cites for it. Then test those exact prompts repeatedly to see whether your mention rate improves.

### What if ChatGPT gets facts about your brand wrong?

You cannot edit ChatGPT's training data directly. Correct the information at the source: your own site, review profiles, directories and any outdated third-party pages, especially the ones cited in search answers. Search-enabled answers can update once corrected pages are retrieved; answers based on older training data may persist until newer models roll out.

## Conclusion

Getting your brand mentioned in ChatGPT comes down to being easy to find, easy to understand and well represented on the sources ChatGPT trusts. Allow OAI-SearchBot, publish clear pages that answer buyer questions, earn coverage and reviews, keep your facts consistent everywhere, and measure your visibility over time.
